Well, 2 and 1/2 months is about 10 weeks. 10x2 = 20 pounds, and it could have been 11 weeks due to estimation (22 pounds). Sounds like a reasonable time frame to me.

When starting any diet, you will lose considerably more weight in the beginning simply due to water and glycogen loss. After about a week or two, weight loss will normalize to a more steady 1-4lbs per week. The heavier you are, the more you'll lose on a weekly basis (good rule of thumb is around 1% of your body weight; so if you're 300lbs, you can realistically expect to lose 3lbs per week).

Also, the claim that it's only healthy to lose 1-2 pounds is not a hard medical fact. It's simply a general recommendation since losing more than that takes A LOT more effort because you either have to maintain a lower daily caloric deficit, or you have to work your ass off in the gym every day (which is hard since you'll want to eat more on workout days). So not impossible or even unhealthy, just unrealistic for most people who are just starting out or are in poor physical shape. Also, consistently losing a smaller amount of weight keeps people motivated over the long term, as opposed to failing to meet higher weight loss goals like 4-5lbs per week.
